analogs.covers: Life: a nocturnal, swimming apex whose males hold a territory that includes the females, with bloody fights between same-sex rivals
How it kills: serrated shark teeth that shear off flesh and let prey bleed out

headline: A nocturnal tiger with a great white shark's bite: booming calls in the dark, then prey bleeding out behind it.

setting.label: Large territories across hills, forests and wetlands
setting.note: Males claim an entire POI as territory and allow one female or female pair inside; females are nomadic until nesting. Strong swimmers that cool off in ponds and the sea.

playsLike: You are an Apex nocturnal carnivore living alone or in a related same-sex pair: brothers or father and son (a 'sett'), sisters or mother and daughter (a 'stand'). Opposite sexes never group, even when nesting. Males hold a whole POI and share kills with the females they allow in. You broadcast loud, haunting calls through the night, hunt any tier (up to 3 on an Argentinosaurus), and bleed prey out with serrated teeth over long pursuits. Rivalries with same-sex Tyrannotitan, Tyrannosaurus and Giganotosaurus are brutal and often lethal.

why.text: Males claim large territories that include a resident female or female pair. Tiger males overlap the ranges of several females in the same way.
Nocturnal, and daylight can even blind it; a strong swimmer that cools off in ponds and the ocean. Tigers are the water-loving night hunters among the big cats.
Only related same-sex pairs group, and opposite sexes meet only to court. Big cats keep this solitary sex split too.

'Rows of sharp teeth that are used to scrape flesh off of the sides of their targets, resulting in deep wounds and hemorrhagic bleeding'. A great white bites and waits for its prey to bleed out, and Tyrannotitan's family literally means 'shark-toothed'.
Apex tier, 5,500 combat weight, 900 HP, sprint 900 held for 63 s.

notLike: Tigers are silent stalkers; Tyrannotitan is usually heard before it is seen.
twist: No official inspiration is listed; this pairing follows its territory system and bite style.
